- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to undercorrect — increase forecast slightly to avoid excessive downward bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overreacts with exaggerated upward momentum — reduce forecast slope or add downward drag.  
- If model consistently forecasts below true mean over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion bias: add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to align with recent trend.  
- When sentiment is positive but model forecasts are flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum — increase forecast by 0.3–0.8% to match sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility — add 0.2–0.5% to final 5–7 days to account for sentiment-driven corrections.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.10 to -0.20), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 0.1–0.3% to avoid overshoot.
